definitions.gloss: timid; faint-hearted; unable to assert oneself
definitions.explanation: Describes someone who cannot say no, backs down under pressure, or is easily rattled. The judgment is usually mildly critical or self-deprecating rather than harsh.

examples.japanese: {弟|おとうと}は{気|き}が{弱|よわ}い。
{気|き}が{弱|よわ}くて{断|ことわ}れなかった。
examples.english: I was too faint-hearted to say no.

examples.japanese: {気|き}の{弱|よわ}い{人|ひと}ほど、{無理|むり}な{仕事|しごと}を{引|ひ}き{受|う}けてしまいがちだ。
examples.english: The more timid a person is, the more likely they are to take on impossible work.

notes:
A fixed {気|き} expression: the subject of {弱|よわ}い is {気|き}, so the person takes は or が in a double-subject pattern ({彼|かれ}は{気|き}が{弱|よわ}い). In attributive position the が becomes の: {気|き}の{弱|よわ}い{人|ひと}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {気|き}の{弱|よわ}い{人|ひと}: a timid person (attributive form)
- {気|き}が{弱|よわ}くて{断|ことわ}れない: too timid to refuse
- {気|き}が{弱|よわ}そう: to look faint-hearted

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {気|き}が{強|つよ}い: strong-willed, assertive — the direct opposite
- {臆病|おくびょう}な: cowardly — about fear itself, stronger and more negative
- {内気|うちき}な: shy, reserved — about reticence with people, not about caving in to pressure

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {気|き}が{弱|よわ}くなかったら
